Doing HTTP ¶ efficiently makes your stuff load faster and saves bandwidth. ¶  ¶ OkHttp is an HTTP client that’s efficient by default: ¶  ¶  * HTTP/2 support allows all requests to the same host to share a socket. ¶  * Connection pooling reduces request latency (if HTTP/2 isn’t available). ¶  * Transparent GZIP shrinks download sizes. ¶  * Response caching avoids the network completely for repeat requests. ¶  ¶ OkHttp perseveres when the network is troublesome: it will silently recover from common connection ¶ problems. If your service has multiple IP addresses, OkHttp will attempt alternate addresses if the ¶ first connect fails. This is necessary for IPv4+IPv6 and services hosted in redundant data ¶ centers. OkHttp supports modern TLS features (TLS 1.3, ALPN, certificate pinning). It can be ¶ configured to fall back for broad connectivity. ¶  ¶ Using OkHttp is easy.
